description: A file cut off while it was being created, at every length up to a new database's size, in both versions. Creating writes the database header, then a root header of zeros, then the trailer of the empty root, and only then the committed size, so what a crash leaves is a prefix of that with no committed size. Since 92a926e such a file, if it's no bigger than a new database, is created again when it's opened: as version 2, even when the cut file was version 1, with the file ID and hash ID given to Database.init, which reopen passes here, and with a hash ID of zeros when it's given none. The cut file's own are lost. Shorter than the database header, it raises EndOfStream. Bigger than a new database, it's a full copy that didn't finish, which opens as a database without a first commit and is left as it is. new_with_hash_id and new_without_hash_id are what a database created again has to be, byte for byte. The port does what the original does here (D31 item 4). Written by src/longscripts.zig.
